column3: The Hebrew names the firmament in the singular; BSB says skies.
The Hebrew makes day and night the subjects speaking to each other; BSB uses they with day after day and night after night.
The Hebrew names their line rather than voice and says in them without explicitly naming the heavens.
The Hebrew says nothing is hidden from its heat; BSB says nothing is deprived of its warmth.
The Hebrew has a singular commandment; BSB uses commandments.
The Hebrew calls them more desirable; BSB says more precious.
The Hebrew does not explicitly supply his own or my before errors and hidden things.
The Hebrew names presumptuous ones without explicitly saying sins; BSB supplies willful sins.
